articles.title: Netherlands Seizes 800 Servers, Arrests 2 for Aiding Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Meta's AI bot got socially engineered harder than a freshman at DefCon, letting attackers seize Obama's Instagram and the Space Force Chief's account. When your AI assistant falls for basic manipulation tactics, maybe it's time to reconsider that whole 'artificial intelligence' label.

articles.title: Alleged Kimwolf Botmaster ‘Dort’ Arrested, Charged in U.S. and Canada
articles.summary: Congress is demanding answers after CISA—the agency literally tasked with cybersecurity—had a contractor leak AWS GovCloud keys on GitHub like a script kiddie's first day. The irony is so thick you could cut it with a rusty exploit.

articles.title: We're Fighting Mass Surveillance Tech—and Winning
articles.summary: A CISA contractor casually dumped AWS GovCloud credentials and internal system access on GitHub for the whole world to see. Nothing says 'cybersecurity leadership' quite like leaving your keys under the digital doormat.

articles.title: Welcome New EFF Executive Director Nicole Ozer
articles.summary: EFF reminds us they're still fighting the good fight against tech-enabled tyranny while we're all busy arguing about AI chatbots. The surveillance state won't defeat itself, folks.

articles.title: DriveSurge Hijacks Thousands of Sites for ClickFix, FakeUpdate Attacks
articles.summary: Police are using license plate readers for everything from school residency checks to noise complaints because mission creep is apparently the only thing law enforcement excels at. Your daily commute is now a constitutional violation waiting to happen.

articles.title: New York Comptroller’s Trip to Israel Raised Ethical Concerns, State Commission Said
articles.summary: Philadelphia cops admit they're tracking 'First Amendment activity' critical of AI data centers. Apparently exercising your constitutional rights makes you a person of interest in the City of Brotherly Love.

articles.title: Claude celebrates Anthropic's stock market float with blockbuster ... outage
articles.summary: Microsoft finally backed down from threatening zero-day researchers after the security community collectively told them to pound sand. Nothing like public humiliation to remind tech giants that bug hunters aren't the enemy.

articles.title: AI-Driven Exploitation is Destroying Vulnerability Management. Here’s How to Handle It.
articles.summary: CISA added Oracle WebLogic CVE-2024-21182 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after active exploitation in the wild. Oracle software getting pwned is about as surprising as water being wet.

articles.title: Anthropic is finally giving the EU access to Mythos, ending weeks of standoff over the world’s most powerful cybersecurity AI
articles.summary: A 9.8-rated Windows Server vulnerability grants system privileges with just a malformed packet, and domain controllers are getting owned in the wild. Microsoft's security track record continues to be a masterclass in creative failure.

articles.title: (2026.06.02) (various)
articles.summary: Anthropic finally gave EU access to Claude Mythos after weeks of standoff—the AI that autonomously discovered 10,000+ zero-days across major operating systems. When your AI finds more bugs than the entire security industry combined, maybe we've been doing this wrong.
